q: What is the degree of (x² + 1)(x³ − x)?
why: The highest powers multiply: x² · x³ = x⁵. Powers add when you multiply.
(x − 3)(x − 3) = x² − 3x − 3x + 9 = x² − 6x + 9. Squaring doesn't split over a minus.

q: Adding two polynomials of degree 3 gives a polynomial of degree 3.
why: The top terms can cancel: (x³ + x) + (−x³ + 1) = x + 1, which has degree 1.
Myth. 1/x = x⁻¹ is a negative power. Polynomials only use whole powers 0, 1, 2, …
